rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 regressed sharply (score 89.8, from 680.0). Its only changes were kp 5.5 to 6.0 and the sensor spread widened from +/-0.06 m to +/-0.08 m. The oval and s-bend went from full completion to 0 finishes, so that candidate is rejected. Iteration 6 (score 680.0) is the stable base: oval 20/20 at 2.08 s, s-bend 20/20 at 2.61 s, slalom 0/20 with progress 0.42 and every failure off track. Iteration 5 (score 680.3) is equivalent in score, so the geometry and controller of iteration 6 are the reference. Across iterations 3 to 6, lowering mass (0.6 to 0.5) and raising kd both reduced steering oscillation and raised slalom progress. The remaining slalom failure is leaving the tape at sharp direction changes, which points to yaw inertia and turn agility rather than damping alone. Change, kept to one lever: mass 0.5 to 0.4 kg, the minimum allowed. This lowers yaw inertia and should speed the response at sharp slalom turns. Everything else is reverted to the iteration-6 geometry (sensors at y=0.08, x = -0.06 to +0.06, sensor_size 0.016, wheel_track 0.10, body 0.16 x 0.12). Controller: kp 5.5, ki 0, kd 2.5, base_speed 1.0, line_loss last_direction. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.5 with some finishes, oval and s-bend completion held (oval time about 2.1 s, s-bend about 2.6 s, both within the 3 s limit), and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.3. Hypotheses: H1, lower mass improves slalom response, shown by slalom progress and line_loss_events improving over iteration 6. H2, if the lighter robot oscillates more on the s-bend, steering_oscillation will rise above 0.2 and kd will need to go higher, which would mean the damping limit is near. H3, if the slalom still fails at its first sharp turn with no change, the limit is authority or sensor reach, and the next lever is kp or the sensor geometry, not mass. Next measurements: progress and completion_time for speed versus stability, max_error and line_loss_events for stability, steering_oscillation for damping, control_effort for gain cost, and noise_robustness for margin on held-back tracks.
